title: Per-path sentinel: adaptive trippoints and deterministic safe-route policy
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a per-path 'sentinel' circuit-breaker layer that computes adaptive trippoints for each request path (dependency/model/tenant combination), enforces deterministic safe-route fallback routing during trips, and integrates with SLO-driven runbooks and multi-region failover policies. Goal: reduce noisy global trips, enable predictable degradations, and ensure application-level correctness during regional or dependency outages.
updates: 2026-03-10: Created ticket with initial design goals and scoped MVP: per-path metrics, adaptive trip algorithm (EWMA+quantiles), and deterministic fallback mapping table.

2026-03-11: Spike completed for per-path metric aggregation. Prototype shows per-tenant P99 latency jitter reduced when trippoints adapt to request mix. Logged prototype results to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/ENG-118005+sentinel-spike

2026-03-12: Design review with PM and SRE. Decision: fallback policy will prefer same-region degraded model variant, then cross-region cold model, then cached-response with cached TTL. Trade-offs discussed: stricter trippoints decrease customer latency but increase fallback frequency; chosen conservative hysteresis to avoid oscillation.

2026-03-13: Engineering implementation started. Initial PR for metric collectors and per-path key computed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3129. Added integration test checklist to ticket.
2026-03-13: Noted dependency on rollout flags infra (ENG-41209) and regional routing table updates (ENG-60217).
acceptance_criteria: Per-path keys generated for all incoming requests (tenant+model+route) and stored in metrics pipeline for 90 days
Adaptive trippoint algorithm computes threshold per path using combination of EWMA and 95th/99th quantile with configurable floor/ceiling

When a path trips, requests are routed deterministically according to fallback policy: (1) same-region compatible variant, (2) preferred cross-region warm pool, (3) cached-response or lightweight heuristic response
Circuit state transitions include durable hysteresis (min-open-time, exponential backoff) and are emitted to observability with distinct metrics (trip_count, open_duration, fallback_rate)
No increase in median latency for non-fallback traffic beyond 2% compared to baseline; fallback traffic provides clear latency/cost tradeoff documentation
Automated chaos test shows safe-route policy preserves correctness of at least 95% of requests for target use-cases during simulated regional outage
Runbook created and linked in Console for SRE and oncall teams, with automated alert thresholds tied to SLO burn-rate
test_plan: Unit tests for trippoint calculator covering edge cases (cold start, low-traffic paths, traffic spikes)
Integration tests that simulate tenant-specific load and verify per-path isolation of trips
Multi-region failover simulation in staging: trigger regional dependency outage and assert deterministic fallback routing and acceptable correctness
Load-shedding validation: under severe overload, ensure shedding respects tenant priorities and SLA tiers
Chaos engineering runbook: scheduled chaos test that toggles dependency health endpoints and asserts graceful recovery
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable sentinel for 5 low-traffic tenants in us-west with read-only metric collection and dry-run fallback decisions
Phase 2 (limited): Activate enforcement for selected model families with conservative trip thresholds and monitor fallback_rate and error budget impact
Phase 3 (regional): Expand to multi-region with warm-pool cross-region routing enabled for gold-tier customers
Phase 4 (global): Full rollout with per-tenant tuning and automated suggestions surfaced in Redwood Console
notes: Algorithm choice rationale: EWMA provides stability for skewed latencies; adding quantile floor/ceiling handles long-tail bursts without catastrophic trips
Fallback ordering rationale: prefer same-region variants to minimize latency and egress cost; cross-region warm pools only used when compatibility and privacy rules permit
Observability: require separate metric streams per path to avoid aggregation masking; tag metrics with 'trip_cause' (latency|errors|capacity)
SLO alignment: trippoints are derived from path-level objective (e.g., P99 < X ms) and calibrated to preserve overall product SLOs while protecting system health
Open question: should tenant-priority be encoded as continuous weight (fractional shedding) or discrete tiers? Will experiment in Phase 2.
